analysis: The only change in docs/architecture/inference.md is a documentation addition (head lines ~1030-1046 per the patch). It describes a new PromptTokenCache in LocalTokenizerBridge, linear-time ChatTemplateLoopRewrites for Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS, and a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 kill switch. The supplied units are the base tail (lines 2017-2205) and the head start (1-415). Neither displays the changed lines 1030-1046, so I could not inspect the new text directly; I only saw the patch excerpt. The documented behavior adds a new in-process cache of prompt token IDs keyed by prefix-cache scope. It states that reuse never crosses a cache scope, that token IDs equal the unchanged applyChatTemplate path's, and that sampled background comparisons disable reuse on a mismatch. This touches A-001 (prompt content held in memory) and is adjacent to T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and the TTFT oracle). The cache's presence is a possible new timing side channel, since cache hits shorten prompt preparation and so TTFT. If scoping is enforced as described, it stays within the accepted same-account SEC-035 residual. The cache holds token IDs in memory only, with no new at-rest artifact stated, and the cache scope is coordinator-authored. Because this PR only changes documentation, I report no regression. The next pass should verify, in the actual source files (PromptTokenCache.swift, ChatTemplateLoopRewrites, LocalTokenizerBridge), that the scope partitioning is enforced, that eviction and bounds exist, that parallel encoding on up to four cores cannot cause resource exhaustion, and that the ChatTemplateLoopRewrites output cannot diverge from the served template. The threat model may also need a note on T-041 about prompt-token reuse timing. The Nemotron Super text in the supplied units appears to be unchanged context.
